title: Tether says it had ‘limited’ exposure to bank linked to $84M US seizure
summary: US prosecutors alleged that a payments business illegally transferred hundreds of millions of dollars at the direction of EQIBank, where Tether holds some assets.
content:
US prosecutors alleged that a payments business illegally transferred hundreds of millions of dollars at the direction of EQIBank, where Tether holds some assets.

Stablecoin issuer Tether said that it had limited exposure through assets held at a bank that reportedly directed a payments company to allegedly move hundreds of millions of dollars on its behalf.

In response to reports linking Tether and Bitfinex to a Montana-based payments business named in a civil forfeiture complaint filed by the Department of Justice, a company spokesperson told Cointelegraph that it had “no knowledge” of any of the alleged conduct. Tether confirmed it was a customer of EQIBank, the bank the Justice Department alleged directed the payments company, Capstone, to send and receive money, but the amount held at the bank represented 0.034% of the group’s total assets.

US prosecutors reportedly froze about $84 million in Capstone’s accounts as part of the complaint. Justice Department officials alleged that the business was unlicensed and had made payments to “hundreds of individuals and entities” on behalf of Tether and Bitfinex, according to the Financial Times.

A Tether spokesperson did not respond to a question about how the seizure could affect its customers. As of Friday, the USDT stablecoin had a market capitalization of about $184 billion.

title: Former Hack VC partner Hsin-Ju Chuang’s death ruled a suicide
summary: The crypto executive and Dystopia Labs founder previously held senior roles at Stellar and Solana before joining venture capital firm Hack VC.
content:
Update (Sept. 25, 18:30 UTC). This article was updated with additional details on Hsin-Ju Chuang’s cause of death.

Hsin-Ju Chuang, a former partner at crypto venture firm Hack VC, died at age 37, according to the San Bernardino County Sheriff-Coroner. The county’s Coroner Death Registry later listed her death as a suicide.

California Highway Patrol officers responded to southbound Interstate 15 south of Field Road in Harvard, California, on Aug. 24, where Chuang was pronounced dead at the scene.

According to her LinkedIn profile, Chuang founded Dystopia Labs and previously served as head of growth at Stellar and Solana. She joined Hack VC as a venture partner in 2021 before becoming partner and head of platform in 2025.

Hack VC co-founder and managing partner Alexander Pack said Wednesday that the firm was “shocked and saddened” by Chuang’s death and offered condolences to her family, friends and others close to her.

Pack said the company had not spoken directly with Chuang for more than 10 months and was not aware of the circumstances surrounding her death. “We have no further information, and only wish to ask everyone to be respectful of those who are grieving,” he added.

Before her death, Chuang had publicly accused Hack VC of mistreating her during her time at the firm and said she intended to release evidence supporting her allegations. In those allegations, Chuang said she had “attempted suicide” after experiencing what she described as mistreatment by the firm while going “through a serious medical emergency.”

title: Best Crypto Staking Platforms for 2026: 7 Options Compared
summary:
Staking is the closest thing crypto has to earning interest: you lock up a proof-of-stake asset to help secure its network, and in return you earn a yield, paid in
The post Best Crypto Staking Platforms for 2026: 7 Options Compared  appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Staking is the closest thing crypto has to earning interest: you lock up a proof-of-stake asset to help secure its network, and in return you earn a yield, paid in more of that asset. It has become one of the most popular ways to put idle crypto to work, but the platforms that offer it vary enormously in the rates they pay, the assets they support, how easily you can unstake, the fees they skim from rewards, and how safe your coins are while they are locked. A headline APY means little if it is a short promotion, if the platform takes a large commission, or if your funds are hard to withdraw when you need them.

This guide compares seven leading staking platforms on what actually determines your net yield and peace of mind: rates and how sustainable they are, asset coverage, flexibility, fees, and security. Every detail was checked against platform documentation and independent trackers, and where access is restricted by region, we say so.

A note on availability: Staking rules differ sharply by region, and some products, including staking, are restricted or unavailable in the United States, the UK, and parts of the EU, so confirm what is offered in your jurisdiction before signing up.

Risk warning: Staking is not risk-free. Rewards can change, locked assets cannot be sold during volatility, and the underlying token can fall in value by more than you earn. This article is informational and is not financial advice.

  • Crypto Staking Platforms at a Glance 
  • How 7 Crypto Staking Platforms Compare 
    • 1. Kraken: Best Platform for Flexible Staking 
    • 2. Coinbase: Best for Easy and Secure Staking 
    • 3. BloFin: Best for Flexible Earn and Stablecoin Yield 
    • 4. Binance: Best for a Wide Range of Products 
    • 5. OKX: Best for DeFi and Web3 Earn 
    • 6. Crypto.com: Best for High Headline Rates  
    • 7. Bybit: Best for Short-Term Promotional Yields 
  • Frequently Asked Questions About Crypto Staking 
  • How to Find the Right Staking Platform 

Crypto Staking Platforms at a Glance 

The table weighs rate, flexibility, and safety together, since the highest advertised number is rarely the best real outcome. Rates are indicative and move constantly, so treat them as a guide and check the live figure.

#PlatformBest forFlexible optionIndicative rate note
1KrakenFlexible staking and breadthYes, plus Auto EarnUp to around 21% on select assets
2CoinbaseOverall ease and securityYesCompetitive, minus a rewards commission
3BloFinFlexible and stablecoin earnYes, plus fixed termsAround 3.5% flexible USDT, higher on fixed
4BinanceProduct variety and depthYesBroad Earn stack across many assets
5OKXDeFi and Web3 earnYesOn-chain plus centralized options
6Crypto.comHighest headline ratesYesUp to around 17.9% APR on select assets
7BybitShort-term promo yieldsYesOccasional high, time-limited campaigns

The right choice depends on whether you want the highest sustainable rate, the easiest experience, or a flexible place to earn on stablecoins, so the profiles below break each one down.

How 7 Crypto Staking Platforms Compare 

1. Kraken: Best Platform for Flexible Staking 

Kraken is widely regarded as the strongest all-round staking platform, particularly for flexible staking where you keep the ability to unstake quickly. It supports a broad range of proof-of-stake assets, advertises rates up to around 21% on select tokens, and its Auto Earn feature puts idle balances to work automatically without you managing each position. Rewards are competitive after fees, and Kraken pairs the product with a long, clean security record that makes locking assets there feel low-risk. The main caveat is that staking availability, like everywhere, depends on your region, so check what is offered locally.

Best for: stakers who want high flexible rates across a broad set of assets from a trusted venue.

Watch out for: the top advertised rates apply only to select assets, and regional restrictions limit what is available.

2. Coinbase: Best for Easy and Secure Staking 

Coinbase is the default for many stakers because it makes the whole process effortless, with one-click staking, a polished app, and the reassurance of a regulated, US-listed operator. Asset coverage is solid across the major proof-of-stake coins, and the security and compliance standards are among the highest here. The trade-off is cost, since Coinbase charges a commission on staking rewards that reduces your net yield, so the effective rate is lower than the headline. For a beginner who values simplicity and safety over squeezing out the last basis point, it is the most comfortable choice.

Best for: beginners who want the simplest, most reassuring staking experience.

Watch out for: a rewards commission trims your net yield below the advertised rate.

3. BloFin: Best for Flexible Earn and Stablecoin Yield 

BloFin approaches earning less as pure proof-of-stake staking and more as a flexible savings suite, which suits people who want to earn on assets they already hold, including stablecoins. Through BloFin Earn you can choose flexible products you can redeem any time or fixed terms of 2 to 180 days that pay more, across assets like USDT, BTC, ETH, and SOL, with flexible USDT around 3.5% and higher rates on locked terms. Its standout is RWUSD, a principal-protected product whose yield is benchmarked against real-world assets such as tokenised Treasury funds, which is an unusual, lower-risk way to earn on stablecoins. You can browse the current products on this crypto staking platform, though for the very highest proof-of-stake APYs on specific tokens, the specialist stakers above pay more.

Best for: users who want flexible earn and a principal-protected stablecoin yield alongside their trading account.

Watch out for: headline proof-of-stake APYs on individual tokens are higher on dedicated staking platforms.

4. Binance: Best for a Wide Range of Products 

Binance offers the broadest earn stack of any exchange here, spanning flexible and locked staking, savings, launchpool, and more, across a huge list of assets. If you want options, from simple flexible staking to more structured products, Binance has the most of them in one place, and rates are competitive across the range. The interface can feel overwhelming given how many products sit side by side, and availability is restricted in a number of jurisdictions, but for sheer variety and asset coverage it is hard to beat.

Best for: experienced users who want the widest choice of earn products and assets.

Watch out for: the sprawling product menu is complex, and access is restricted in several regions.

5. OKX: Best for DeFi and Web3 Earn 

OKX stands out for bridging centralized staking with on-chain DeFi through its integrated Web3 wallet, so you can move from simple exchange staking to higher-yield DeFi strategies without leaving the ecosystem. It supports flexible and locked products across the major assets, and the Web3 tools open access to on-chain yields that pure exchanges do not offer. That extra reach comes with extra complexity and the usual smart-contract risks of DeFi, and full verification is required upfront, so it suits more hands-on users than absolute beginners.

Best for: users who want centralized staking plus access to on-chain DeFi yields.

Watch out for: DeFi strategies add smart-contract risk, and the platform requires full verification.

6. Crypto.com: Best for High Headline Rates  

Crypto.com regularly advertises some of the highest staking rates in the market, up to around 17.9% APR on select assets, which draws yield-focused users. The best rates are often tied to locking the platform’s own token or to promotional tiers, so the effective rate for a casual staker can be lower than the top-line figure suggests. Asset coverage and the app experience are strong, and it remains a popular choice for those chasing yield, provided you read the conditions attached to the headline number.

Best for: yield-focused users willing to meet the conditions attached to the top rates.

Watch out for: the highest rates often depend on token lock-ups or promotions, so the effective yield can be lower.

7. Bybit: Best for Short-Term Promotional Yields 

Bybit periodically runs eye-catching yield campaigns, sometimes advertising very high figures on new-listing or promotional products, alongside a standard flexible savings offering. These promotions can be genuinely attractive for a short window, but they are usually capped, time-limited, or restricted to specific assets, so they are best treated as a bonus rather than a base strategy. For everyday staking Bybit is competent rather than a leader, and its main strength remains derivatives rather than earn.

Best for: active Bybit users who want to opportunistically catch a promotional yield.

Watch out for: the headline promo rates are temporary and capped, so they are not a reliable base yield.

Frequently Asked Questions About Crypto Staking 

What is staking, and how does it pay a yield? Staking locks a proof-of-stake token to help validate its network, and in return you earn newly issued tokens as a reward. Exchange staking does this on your behalf, so you earn without running a validator yourself. Kraken’s learning hub has a clear beginner explainer.

Is a higher APY always better? No. A high advertised rate can be a short promotion, can depend on locking a platform token, or can be eroded by a rewards commission, so compare the sustainable net rate rather than the headline. A steady 5% you actually receive beats an advertised 20% you never fully capture.

Can I lose money staking? Yes, in two ways. The token you stake can fall in price by more than you earn, and locked terms can prevent you from selling during a sharp drop. Coinbase’s learning resources cover the risks in plain language.

What is the difference between flexible and fixed staking? Flexible products let you unstake any time and pay a lower rate, while fixed or locked products tie your asset up for a set term in exchange for a higher rate. Match the choice to whether you might need the funds before the term ends.

How to Find the Right Staking Platform 

  1. Compare net rates, not headlines. Subtract commissions and ignore short promotions, since the sustainable rate you actually receive is what matters.
  2. Decide how much flexibility you need. If you might sell soon, favor flexible products or a shorter fixed term over a long lock-up.
  3. Weigh security and regulation. You are handing custody of a locked asset to the platform, so a long track record and strong compliance matter more here than on a quick trade.
  4. Match the product to the asset. For proof-of-stake coins, a dedicated staker like Kraken or Coinbase leads, while for stablecoins a flexible earn product or a principal-protected option is often the better fit.

The bottom line: Kraken leads on flexible staking and Coinbase on ease and security, while BloFin is a strong pick for flexible earn and principal-protected stablecoin yield, Binance and OKX for product depth, and Crypto.com and Bybit for chasing the highest, if more conditional, rates.

summary:
Bitget has raised its estimate of assets transferred to attacker-controlled addresses from $351.6 million to $387.5 million, adding transfers through Zcash and TRON that were missing from the first calculation.
London's trading industry is coming home!
The revised figure is about 83.5% of its User P...
content:
2026-09-25T19:30:00.000+02:00

Friday, 25/09/2026 | 17:30 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • A full payout from the fund would leave about $76.5 million, below Bitget’s stated $300 million commitment.
  • Bitget has frozen some stolen assets but has not disclosed the amount recovered or how compensation will be funded.

Bitget has raised its estimate of assets transferred to attacker-controlled addresses from $351.6 million to $387.5 million, adding transfers through Zcash and TRON that were missing from the first calculation.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The revised figure is about 83.5% of its User Protection Fund, based on the exchange’s stated valuation of more than $464 million. Bitget would then need to replenish the reserve to restore it above its stated $300 million commitment.

The calculation remains hypothetical because frozen or recovered assets could reduce the amount ultimately required from the fund.

[SECURITY NOTICE] Bitget Hot Wallet Incident — September 24, 2026

At 18:31 UTC on September 24, 2026, Bitget's security systems detected unauthorized transfers from some of our hot wallets. Our security team activated emergency response protocols immediately.

What we have…

— Gracy Chen @Bitget (@GracyBitget) September 24, 2026

Fund Value Moves with Bitcoin

Bitget established the Protection Fund in 2022 to cover losses from hacks and other extreme events, such as the September 24 breach of part of its hot- and warm-wallet infrastructure.

The fund holds 5,500 Bitcoin and is separate from the reserves backing customer balances. Bitget says the incident falls within its coverage. Its dollar value fluctuates with Bitcoin.

The fund averaged $382 million in August, ranging from $345.3 million to $441.5 million, according to Bitget’s latest monthly report.

Frozen Assets May Reduce the Final Cost

Mandiant and SlowMist are assisting with the investigation and security checks. Bitget said it has identified the attack path and remediated the underlying vulnerability, with no further unauthorised transfers possible.

We’re working closely with @bitget on the ongoing investigation. For further details, please refer to Bitget’s official updates. https://t.co/bFckgAnS9I

— SlowMist (@SlowMist_Team) September 25, 2026

Some of the transferred assets have been frozen through coordination with exchanges, blockchain projects and security firms. Bitget has also launched a recovery bounty offering eligible participants 5% of assets they help freeze or recover.

Actions taken under court orders, law-enforcement requests or other legal processes do not qualify.

CEO Gracy Chen said Bitget also holds more than $1 billion of its own assets; however, it did not say how any payments would be divided between the Protection Fund and its own assets.

The value of frozen or recovered assets, the compensation timetable, or how quickly the fund would be replenished are also undisclosed. The status and timing of restored withdrawals will be announced by 04:00 UTC on September 26.

Fund Size Is Not Tied to Disclosed Wallet Exposure

No uniform international formula determines how large a voluntary crypto exchange protection fund should be.

A fixed headline amount does not show its relationship to assets held in online wallets, customer liabilities, the potential loss from a single breach or the liquidity of the reserve.

South Korea provides one risk-based benchmark. Its rules require virtual asset providers to obtain insurance or hold reserves equal to at least 5% of customer assets stored outside cold wallets, subject to a minimum amount.

The benchmark cannot be applied directly to Bitget because the exchange does not publish the value of customer assets held in its hot and warm wallets.

For comparison, Binance maintains a SAFU reserve valued at approximately $1 billion. Like Bitget’s fund, it is held in Bitcoin, and its dollar value therefore changes with the cryptocurrency’s price.

title: Ledger Opens 24/7 Tokenized Stocks to Millions With xStocks Integration
summary:
Key Takeaways: Ledger and a new partnership with Payward have brought xStocks to the Ledger wallet ecosystem. Eligible Ledger holders can trade hundreds of U.S. and worldwide stocks without any
The post Ledger Opens 24/7 Tokenized Stocks to Millions With xStocks Integration appeared first on CryptoN...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Ledger and a new partnership with Payward have brought xStocks to the Ledger wallet ecosystem.
  • Eligible Ledger holders can trade hundreds of U.S. and worldwide stocks without any custodial requirements.
  • In crypto, xStocks now has over $42 billion of transactions to its credit, indicating how fast tokenized equities are growing, says Payward.

Tokenized stocks are increasingly embedding in crypto’s self-custody ecosystem. Payward, the company behind xStocks and parent of Kraken, has teamed up with Ledger to bring hundreds of tokenized equities to Ledger Wallet, giving eligible users onchain access to stocks beyond traditional market hours.

xStocks is now live on @Ledger.

Through Payward’s new partnership with Ledger, we’re bringing hundreds of US and international tokenized equities to Ledger Wallet™.

24/7 market access for millions of Ledger users. pic.twitter.com/XE3bugy7Me

— xStocks (@xStocksFi) September 24, 2026

  • xStocks Lands Inside Ledger Wallet
  • $42B xStocks Volume Sets the Scale
    • Tokenized Equities Move Into Self-Custody
    • xStocks Pushes Beyond U.S. Stocks

xStocks Lands Inside Ledger Wallet

The integration links two marketplaces, transforming the Ledger’s environment of hardware-backed custody into Payward’s market xStocks. Users who qualify are allowed to purchase, sell and pass on supported tokenized equities without having to compromise on their wallet keys.

The integration includes hundreds of tokenized equities from U.S. and global markets, Payward said. According to the company, xStocks are 1:1-backed representations of publicly traded shares, with the aim of moving beyond blockchain-enabled transfers and instantaneous market access for equity exposure.

But the partnership introduces an extra layer of security for Kraken users. The only transactions that are supported might need to be signed by a Ledger device and require a physical confirmation before assets move.

Read More: Kraken Launches xStocks Vaults With Up to 2% Yield on Tokenized Stocks and ETFs Now

$42B xStocks Volume Sets the Scale

Payward claimed xStocks has reached over $42 billion in transaction volumes combined. The number does not represent XSTH sizes owned by users on Ledger but the amount of activity held on the xStocks ecosystem.

xStocks is also spread out on intent trading venues. On the HyperCore, five different tokenized U.S. stocks and ETFs went live in August, bringing the framework to a native spot-market order-book environment.

Tokenized Equities Move Into Self-Custody

With the integration of the Ledger, users will now have the possibility to store their tokenized stocks. Eligible users are now able to interact with trading and transaction services while self-custody using Ledger’s infrastructure.

Especially in the context of crypto users who are used to managing their own private keys. Ledger’s hardware wallets have ensured that signing credentials have been kept separate from Internet connections, and transactions are still authorized by the individual on the device.

The companies are trying to link self-custody to trading and the wider financial system, Payward co-CEO David Ripley said.

xStocks Pushes Beyond U.S. Stocks

Payward is broadening its focus from the U.S. equity market to other stocks. The company joined with GTN to expand it to international equities in July, starting with assets listed on the Hong Kong exchange before moving onto other markets, such as the U.K., Europe and South Korea.

The partnership also included the London Stock Exchange in September to conduct research into the possibility of tokenizing public equities and launching trading on LSE 24 (upon regulatory approval).

The addition means that the growing, tokenized-equity economy is accessible to Ledger users alongside cryptocurrencies in their self-custody wallets.

title: Google’s Space AI Data Centres Raise New Questions as Pope Leo Warns of a Threat to Humanity
summary: Google is preparing to test whether artificial intelligence infrastructure can operate in space, placing specialized Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) aboard a satellite as part of Project Suncatcher.
content:
Skip to content

Google is preparing to test whether artificial intelligence infrastructure can operate in space, placing specialized Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) aboard a satellite as part of Project Suncatcher.

Google’s research initiative examines whether low Earth orbit could eventually support scalable machine learning infrastructure powered by solar energy.

The experiment comes as Pope Leo XIV has intensified his warnings about the social and ethical consequences of artificial intelligence. During his visit to France on September 25, the pope cautioned that AI could contribute to a future in which a “paradise of machines” undermines human agency and daily life.

Google’s Project Suncatcher will send four Trillium TPUs into orbit aboard a SpaceX Transporter-18 mission with Planet to test their resilience to radiation, thermal extremes, and launch vibration. Source: Google via X

The two developments address different sides of the same rapidly expanding technology. Google is investigating how to increase the physical capacity available for AI computing, while Pope Leo is emphasizing how that growing capability should be governed and directed.

Google says Project Suncatcher remains a research effort rather than an operational space-based AI data center. The immediate objective is to determine whether its hardware can withstand the demanding conditions of orbit and whether the engineering challenges can eventually be overcome.

Hardware survival

Project Suncatcher’s first orbital test is being developed with satellite company Planet and is scheduled to fly on SpaceX’s Transporter-18 rideshare mission. The mission will collect data on how Google’s TPUs respond to launch forces, radiation, and extreme thermal conditions in space.

Space-based AI infrastructure could harness near-constant sunlight in low Earth orbit, generating up to eight times more solar power for large-scale workloads. Source: Google via X

Launch itself presents a significant mechanical challenge. Google says a spacecraft can experience acceleration of up to about 10 times Earth’s gravity during its journey to low Earth orbit, while individual components can encounter substantially higher forces. Engineers therefore subjected the satellite hardware to vibration testing across three axes to reproduce conditions associated with a rocket launch.

Radiation represents another concern. Outside Earth’s atmosphere, electronics are exposed to solar events and cosmic rays that can cause errors in computing systems. Google tested its Trillium TPUs at the UC Davis Crocker Nuclear Laboratory using a proton beam while the chips were running AI workloads.

According to Google, initial testing indicated that the Trillium TPUs could withstand a total ionizing radiation dose greater than the amount expected during a five-year space mission. The orbital test is intended to determine how those results translate into actual operating conditions.

Google introduced Trillium as its sixth-generation TPU in 2024. The company says the chip delivers 4.7 times the peak compute performance per chip of its previous TPU v5e generation and is more than 67% more energy efficient.

Cooling in space

Operating AI data centres in orbit creates a separate engineering problem: removing heat.

AI accelerators generate substantial amounts of heat, but conventional cooling systems often depend on moving air or liquid through equipment. In the vacuum of space, there is no atmosphere to carry heat away through ordinary airflow.

Google says its Project Suncatcher team is testing heat pipes and radiators to manage thermal loads. The company has already conducted experiments inside a thermal vacuum chamber designed to reproduce the conditions that electronics would experience in orbit.

io.net argues decentralized compute can reduce centralized bottlenecks and control constraints, offering a practical GPU-based alternative for AI workloads. Source: @ionet via X

The cooling question is particularly important for any future attempt to scale space-based AI infrastructure. A constellation carrying larger numbers of TPUs would need to continuously manage the heat generated by those processors while maintaining reliable performance.

Energy availability is one of the main reasons Google is investigating the concept. The company says satellites in low Earth orbit can receive near-constant sunlight and potentially generate up to eight times more solar power than equivalent solar panels on Earth.

That does not mean orbital AI data centres are ready to replace terrestrial facilities. Google describes Suncatcher as a long-term research project, with the current mission focused on gathering engineering data rather than deploying commercial computing capacity.

Satellite interconnectivity

Scaling AI computing beyond a single satellite would require multiple spacecraft to operate as a coordinated network. Google is therefore also examining how satellites could exchange large volumes of data while moving rapidly around Earth.

The company’s proposed architecture would place multiple TPU chips on individual satellites and connect spacecraft using optical laser links. Google says future satellites would need to determine their own positions and those of neighboring spacecraft with extremely high precision to maintain these connections.

The company plans to test this technology during a two-satellite mission in 2027. The objective is to investigate whether high-bandwidth, short-distance laser communications can provide the connectivity required for distributed AI processing in orbit.

The concept builds on Google’s original Project Suncatcher announcement in November 2025, when the company described a potential network of solar-powered satellites equipped with TPUs. At that stage, Google said its research included satellite constellation design, control, communications, and radiation testing.

The broader AI infrastructure market is simultaneously expanding on Earth. Google has continued to invest in conventional TPU capacity as demand for machine learning computing grows. In May 2026, Google and Blackstone announced a planned TPU cloud venture with an initial $5 billion equity commitment and an expected 500 megawatts of capacity coming online in 2027.

That contrast highlights the experimental nature of Suncatcher: Google is expanding terrestrial AI infrastructure while separately examining whether some future computing workloads could operate beyond the planet.

Just the beginning

Google’s Project Suncatcher is still at an early research stage. The immediate test is not designed to demonstrate a commercial space-based AI data center but to establish whether the underlying hardware and supporting systems can function reliably in orbit.

The project also reflects a broader challenge facing the AI industry: expanding computing capacity while dealing with energy, cooling, communications, and infrastructure requirements. Google’s approach is to investigate whether access to continuous sunlight and orbital infrastructure could eventually provide another way to scale machine learning systems.

Pope Leo called for international AI governance, warning that a “paradise of machines” could erode human ethical judgment and urging greater education in responsible technology use. Source: Reuters via X

Pope Leo’s concerns focus on a different dimension of that expansion. In his September 25 address in France, he warned against losing human agency as AI becomes increasingly integrated into daily life, saying there was an “urgent need for education in ethical discernment.”

His position is also outlined in Magnifica Humanitas, his May 2026 encyclical on safeguarding the human person in the age of artificial intelligence. The Vatican document argues that AI should remain subject to human responsibility and oversight while recognizing its potential benefits. It also highlights the energy and resource demands associated with increasingly powerful AI systems.

The Vatican has therefore framed AI governance not simply as a technical issue but as a question involving human dignity, accountability, and the common good. In the encyclical, Leo argues that technological progress should remain directed toward human welfare rather than allowing efficiency or economic power to become the sole measure of progress.

Google’s space research and Pope Leo’s warnings do not directly address the same problem. One concerns the physical limits of AI infrastructure; the other concerns the social and ethical limits of increasingly powerful technology. Together, however, they illustrate how the next phase of AI development is expanding beyond model performance to questions about energy, infrastructure, governance, and humanity’s role in directing the technology.

summary:
Key Takeaways: KelpDAO is suing LayerZero and co-founder Bryan Pellegrino for the April attack that resulted in 116,500 rsETH valued at approximately $292 million. According to KelpDAO, LayerZero has not
The post KelpDAO Sues LayerZero Over $292M rsETH Exploit, Turning a DeFi Feud Into Court Battle ...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • KelpDAO is suing LayerZero and co-founder Bryan Pellegrino for the April attack that resulted in 116,500 rsETH valued at approximately $292 million.
  • According to KelpDAO, LayerZero has not reported key vulnerabilities; nor have it made efforts to secure its infrastructure used by its verification system.
  • LayerZero has walked back KelpDAO’s claim, citing its 1-of-1 DVN settings as a factor in the exploits.

KelpDAO’s feud with LayerZero has crossed over from rhetoric and technical papers to law courts. The lawsuit is focused on the attack that drained 116,500 rsETH from KelpDAO’s LayerZero bridge in April and serves as a precursor to an ongoing source of tension between cross-chain security providers.

KelpDAO Takes LayerZero Dispute to Court

KelpDAO announced on Sept. 25 that it had filed a lawsuit against LayerZero and Bryan Pellegrino, LayerZero’s co-founder and CEO. The case seeks to hold the defendants responsible for losses and damage that KelpDAO says resulted from the exploit.

https://t.co/D17UbUbixh

— Kelp (@KelpDAO) September 25, 2026

KelpDAO claims LayerZero did not reveal vulnerabilities and risks in its tech and was unable to protect against attackers exploiting infrastructure usage during the verification. The charges have not been substantiated in court.

Pellegrino has dismissed the lawsuit as frivolous and vowed to fight it out in Vancouver. So the issue of the law is the different sides’ perceptions of how the bridge had been made vulnerable.

The $292M rsETH Exploit

In all an attacker stole 116,500 rsETH, which at the time of the incident had a total value of approximately $292 million. According to LayerZero’s investigation, the attacker began to social engineer its way into the hands of a LayerZero developer, before infiltrating its RPC system.

The híjacked infrastructure provided defrauded data on the blockchain to LayerZero’s verification system. This enabled a malformed cross chain message to get a valid attestation.

The attackers did not exploit known vulnerabilities in KelpDAO’s smart contracts, as it was shown by Chainalysis. The false message eventually led to the release of rsETH, without any token burn in the source chain.

Why the 1-of-1 DVN Setup Is Central

According to LayerZero, KelpDAO’s rsETH was linked to a 1-of-1 Decentralized Verifier Network (DVN), where LayerZero Labs was the only verifier.

LayerZero says that had resulted in a single point of failure. If the verifier had been compromised by this attacker, there was no independent verifier to reject the forged message. LayerZero has said it had recommended multi-DVN redundancy.

KelpDAO denies that and states that it has been read and approved by LayerZero in writing to be deployed and configured. It’s a controversial assertion in the litigation.

Read More: BonkDAO Hit by $20M Treasury Hack After Malicious Governance Proposal Rocks BONK Holders

KelpDAO Moves rsETH Away From LayerZero

Following the exploit, KelpDAO shifted its focus to ensuring cross-chain security of its system. The protocol was rolled out to move the rsETH bridge away from the LayerZero layer-two infrastructure and into Chainlink CCIP.

LayerZero also responded to the incident by removing support of 1-of-1 DVN configurations for compromised applications and strengthening its infrastructure related to the attack.

The lawsuit now puts those technical disagreements under judicial scrutiny, with the key questions including responsibility for the compromised infrastructure, the bridge configuration, and the security warnings provided before the $292 million exploit.

title: Binance Bitcoin Outflows Hit 13,800 BTC in 3-Year Record as FOMO Returns
summary:
Key Takeaways: More than 13,800 BTC was out, a record amount of money in a single day for Binance since 2023. Binance’s Bitcoin reserves fell by roughly 20,000 BTC in
The post Binance Bitcoin Outflows Hit 13,800 BTC in 3-Year Record as FOMO Returns appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • More than 13,800 BTC was out, a record amount of money in a single day for Binance since 2023.
  • Binance’s Bitcoin reserves fell by roughly 20,000 BTC in four days, from 705,000 BTC to 685,000 BTC.
  • According to CryptoQuant analyst Darkfrost, the aggressive withdrawals were a result of renewed accumulation and perhaps FOMO among investors returning to Bitcoin.

Bitcoin is seeing a sharp shift in exchange flows while its latest rally continues. CryptoQuant data cited by analyst Darkfrost shows that traders are pulling unusually large amounts of BTC from Binance, pointing to a major change in how market participants are positioning their coins.

Binance sees record Outflows since 2023 amid Bitcoin FOMO 🟢

Bitcoin has entered a bullish dynamic that’s different from previous rebounds. Since it’s high in July, BTC has delivered a performance of roughly 45%. This rally notably broke through an important structural point,… pic.twitter.com/jIqyIvdKXt

— Darkfost (@Darkfost_Coc) September 25, 2026

  • Binance Sees Its Biggest BTC Outflow Since 2023
  • Outflows Do Not Automatically Mean Accumulation
    • Bitcoin Rally Adds Fuel to the Withdrawal Wave
    • Latecomer FOMO Enters the Bitcoin Market

Binance Sees Its Biggest BTC Outflow Since 2023

The key player here is the 13,800-plus BTC that exited Binance in 1 day. According to Darkfrost, this was the largest net Bitcoin flow out of the exchange since 2023.

This change doesn’t have to be limited to one session. Binance’s netflow has been negative and averaged around 2,000 BTC per week, with its reported BTC holding reducing from ~705,000 to ~685,000 BTC over four days.

Darkfrost says Binance accounts for approximately 30% of the Bitcoin residing in all exchanges within all investors’ reach. This creates a stark difference in its exchange balance, especially in how fast it moves as on-chain market watchers track it.

CryptoQuant offers exchange flow and reserve data which detail the movement of cryptocurrencies across exchanges and other wallets.

Read More: Strategy Sells Bitcoin for First Time Since 2022 While Still Holding 843,706 BTC

Outflows Do Not Automatically Mean Accumulation

When BTC is removed from an exchange, this doesn’t expose the owner’s intentions, as well as removing the stock that may be open to trade.

Coins may go to private custodial wallets or institutional custody, other exchanges, or other arrangements in internal storage. For this reason, exchange outflows are more likely a sort of supply-flow checker than evidence of an imminent long-term buying spree by investors.

Bitcoin Rally Adds Fuel to the Withdrawal Wave

What caught the attention on the latest data is the timing of the Binance withdrawals. Bitcoin is up about 45% from its position in July and has found a resistance point at $82,000 as it has closed back above multiple times, Darkfrost said. The analyst continues to view BTC accumulation going on despite the rising prices.

It gives rise to a different market environment than a coin-flow and then just to exchanges for active trading.

Rather, Bitcoin is climbing while a massive amount of BTC is simultaneously exiting one of the largest industry trading venues. If they’re not part of exchanges, there is less available on Binance immediately.

Read More: Binance Wallet Opens $4.7T Pre-IPO Market Access Through PancakeSwap Tokenized Deals

Latecomer FOMO Enters the Bitcoin Market

Another reason for extremely high withdrawals from Darkfrost, is the fact that people may have been waiting for a correction before getting back into the game if they were late.

The early phase of the bull market may have been too challenging for investors who saw BTC plummet before. When price levels are conquered by a strong hike, that behavior can flip rapidly, needing these side line clients to bid up.

The result can be a feedback loop in which rising prices attract new demand while existing holders move BTC away from exchanges.

content:
2026-09-25T17:54:36.953+02:00

Friday, 25/09/2026 | 15:54 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Administrative expenses rose to £6.20 million, pushing the company into an operating loss.
  • Interest income of £97,267 helped offset the operating loss during the year.

Hantec Markets Limited, UK, reported a slight decline in turnover and lower annual profit for 2025, despite an increase in profit before tax.

For the year ended 31 December 2025, the UK-based company recorded turnover of £6.19 million, down from £6.21 million a year earlier. This represents a decline of about 0.3%.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Administrative expenses rose to £6.20 million, compared with £6.13 million in 2024. The increase pushed the company from an operating profit of £82,362 in 2024 to an operating loss of £7,726 in 2025.

Hantec Markets Profit Falls Despite Higher Pre-Tax

The operating loss was offset by £97,267 in interest receivable and similar income. The company also had no interest payable or similar expenses during the year, compared with £2,612 in 2024.

As a result, profit before taxation increased to £89,541, from £79,750 a year earlier.

After a tax charge of £41,342, Hantec Markets reported a profit for the financial year of £48,199, down from £72,350 in 2024.

The financial statements state that the income statement was prepared on the basis that “all operations are continuing.”

Directors remained cautious about the outlook. "Market conditions will be challenging in 2026," they noted, "but we still expect to improve profitability." The firm's strategy remained focused on the long term.

Hantec Adds Copy Trading Technology

Separately, Hantec Markets has continued to expand its trading services through technology partnerships. The broker integrated Brokeree Solutions’ technology for its Hantec Social copy trading platform and Hantec PAMM managed account service across MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5.

Hantec had previously launched its PAMM service using Brokeree’s infrastructure. The broker also integrated Swiset’s analytics and trader engagement tools, adding further technology services for its clients.

title: Bitcoin Treasury Strategy Proposes Daily Dividends For Preferred Stocks
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Treasury Strategy Proposes Daily Dividends For Preferred Stocks
Strategy stockholders are being asked to attend a meeting to approve daily dividends on STRF, STRC, STRK, and STRD. 
This post Bitcoin Treasury Strategy Proposes Daily Dividends For Preferred Stocks first appea...
content:
Bitcoin treasury company Strategy wants to pay investors daily dividends on four of its preferred stocks.

The largest corporate holder of bitcoin said Friday that it was asking shareholders to approve the move, which would pay investors dividends every calendar day — including weekends and holidays — on STRF, STRC, STRK, and STRD. 

“If approved and adopted, we believe this would reduce reinvestment lag, enhance liquidity and market efficiency, and increase price stability,” Strategy said in a statement. Stockholders will attend a meeting to vote on the proposal on October 28. 

Strategy slowed down with its aggressive bitcoin buys this year, as the largest cryptocurrency fell into a bear market. The Nasdaq-listed company instead focused on protecting its balance sheet and sold chunks of its bitcoin. 

Friday’s announcement claimed the move would help both investors and common stockholders. 

“We believe these enhancements can also benefit our common stockholders by increasing the attractiveness and utility of our Digital Credit instruments, supporting our ability to access preferred equity capital efficiently and expanding the capital markets toolkit we use to execute our Bitcoin Treasury strategy,” Strategy added in a statement. 

Strategy — formerly MicroStrategy — is an enterprise software company that pivoted to buying and holding bitcoin in 2020. 

It first bought the cryptocurrency to protect its shareholders from inflation. Since then, it has aggressively bought the asset and pivoted to being a bitcoin treasury. 

Investors can now buy its shares to get heightened exposure to the cryptocurrency, or get paid a yield via its digital credit products. 

The company would buy bitcoin every Monday but slowed down its buys after announcing a program under which it may sell BTC  from time to time to generate up to $1.25 billion in proceeds for the USD reserve, additionally fund preferred stock dividends and interest expenses or fund repurchases. 

Strategy said in a filing Monday that it last week bought 950 bitcoins for $75.7 million — its first buy since August. 

Its Nasdaq-listed stock (MSTR) is down nearly 50% over the past year after the price of bitcoin took a hit. 

But since the company started buying bitcoin in 2020, MSTR has appreciated by nearly 1,000%. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Bitget Halts Withdrawals After $351.6M Hot Wallet Incident Hits Crypto Exchange
summary:
Key Takeaways: Bitget reported unauthorized transactions of about $351.6 million that occurred in a portion of its hot & warm wallet infrastructure. Withdrawals were put on hold for the time
The post Bitget Halts Withdrawals After $351.6M Hot Wallet Incident Hits Crypto Exchange appeared first on Cr...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Bitget reported unauthorized transactions of about $351.6 million that occurred in a portion of its hot & warm wallet infrastructure.
  • Withdrawals were put on hold for the time being as the exchange’s security team examined the situation.
  • Bitget Wallet separately reminded the users to revoke the current permissions of contracts as a precautionary protocol for investigation.

On September 24, Bitget reported some unauthorized transfers from its hot wallets to be one of the biggest crypto security incidents of 2026. The exchange told reporters that its cold wallets are still solid and deposits and trading are still working.

  • $351.6M Moved From Bitget Wallet Infrastructure
  • Bitget Wallet Users Told to Revoke Contract Approvals
    • Investigation Turns to the Attack Route
    • Crypto Exchange Security Under the Spotlight

$351.6M Moved From Bitget Wallet Infrastructure

Bitget said its security systems detected abnormal transfers at 18:31 UTC on September 24 and triggered its emergency response procedures within minutes. The exchange estimates that about $351.6 million was affected.

Live about Bitget Hot Wallet Incident on September 24, 2026 https://t.co/limZaY2pRf

— Bitget (@bitget) September 24, 2026

The event only affected parts of the company’s hot and warm wallet layers, the company claimed. The official security notice states that its cold wallets did not get affected. Bitget also noted that the funds in users’ accounts stayed correct, and the affected amount is protected by its User Protection Fund, which exceeds $464 million.

Withdrawals are suspended while a security review is carried out. Bitget’s recent update says that trading and deposits were still open. The exchange revealed that it has detected and marked abnormal receiving addresses and informed police and blockchain security firms.

Read More: Revolut Exposes Bitcoin Records, Passports After Fraudulent Government Email Attack

Bitget Wallet Users Told to Revoke Contract Approvals

The incident also issued another word of caution in regards to Bitget Wallet users.

BitGet has urged users to stop the activation of their trades until more information is provided. If access to some tokens is not required, then unneeded permissions can lower the chances of exposure for an unwanted contract interaction. Bitget’s own security advice suggests visiting the approval logs to cancel permissions no longer required.

Furthermore, Bitget Wallet has announced that it is not affected by the incident with its own wallet systems and user assets, adding that its self-custody wallet infrastructure is independent of the custody wallet network of the exchange.

Investigation Turns to the Attack Route

For now, Bitget hasn’t publicly announced the specific flaw that enabled the unauthorized transfers. The exchange didn’t reveal any more details about the attack vector in its official notification till investigations are complete.

Later, Gracy Chen, the company’s CEO, said the preliminary investigation showed IP addresses that could have been related to VPN services owned by a DPRK-backed hacking group. It was an investigative clue and not an attribution that had been finalized, she said.

Onchain analysts have seen assets pouring into new addresses and being traded betweenDEXs. But it does not map possible movements of the blockchain to tractor owners or the manner in which the initial break-in was made.

Crypto Exchange Security Under the Spotlight

The incident points to the difference of hot wallets, warm wallets and cold storage in centralized crypto exchanges.

Hot wallets remain connected to systems that facilitate transactions, making them useful for day-to-day withdrawals but also exposing them to a larger online attack surface. Cold wallets are kept offline or otherwise isolated from routine online operations.

Bitget said the investigation is ongoing and that it plans to publish a full incident report covering the root cause and corrective actions. The exchange has also said withdrawals will resume after its security review is completed.

title: Coincheck Launches 2x Crypto CFDs Six Years After Ending Margin Trading
summary:
Japanese cryptocurrency exchange Coincheck has staged a comeback in crypto derivatives more than six years after closing its previous margin product.
London's trading industry is coming home!

The company’s new leveraged trading service, “Coincheck Leverage, is not a revival of Coincheck’s former le...
content:
2026-09-25T15:35:06.799+02:00

Friday, 25/09/2026 | 13:35 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Coincheck has returned to leveraged crypto trading with cash-settled CFDs on Bitcoin, Ether and XRP, capped at 2x leverage.
  • The new service uses a regulated derivatives account rather than the lending model Coincheck discontinued in 2020.

Japanese cryptocurrency exchange Coincheck has staged a comeback in crypto derivatives more than six years after closing its previous margin product.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The company’s new leveraged trading service, “Coincheck Leverage, is not a revival of Coincheck’s former lending-based margin model. It operates under the regulatory model of contracts for difference (CFDs).

How Coincheck Leverage Works

Coincheck began rolling out the service to eligible individual customers on September 24. The available pairs are BTC/JPY, ETH/JPY, and XRP/JPY, and users can take both long and short positions.

Retail clients must provide margin equal to 50% of their position, limiting leverage to twice the deposited amount. The service supports market, limit and stop orders and trades around the clock outside maintenance periods.

The CFDs settle gains and losses in cash without transferring or lending the underlying cryptocurrency. Coincheck disclosed plans for the product in Coincheck Group’s annual report.

The service is now offered under the company’s Type I Financial Instruments Business registration, number 3540, with the Kanto Local Finance Bureau. Japan requires this registration for businesses conducting over-the-counter crypto derivatives transactions.

Spot and CFD Trading Share One App

Coincheck has integrated the CFDs into its existing application. Customers can switch between spot and leveraged trading without downloading a separate app and transfer Japanese yen between the two services. The accounts remain separate.

Customers must already have a Coincheck spot account and open an additional Coincheck Leverage account, which requires a suitability assessment.

The CFDs are initially available through version 5.0.0 or later of the iOS app, with access expanding gradually among eligible users. According to the launch announcement, Android and web versions are planned before the end of 2026, while corporate accounts are scheduled to receive access from 2027.

Previous Product Relied on Borrowing

Coincheck’s former margin product used a different structure. Customers borrowed yen or crypto assets for trading within the platform, with Coincheck connecting participants seeking to lend and borrow yen or Bitcoin.

The exchange stopped accepting new borrowing in May 2017 and closed the remaining service on March 13, 2020. Existing customers were instructed to repay their outstanding positions before the closure.

Coincheck did not disclose a reason for ending the product. At the time, it said only that it was considering an alternative service.

The new CFD offering provides leveraged price exposure through a regulated derivatives account rather than reviving the previous borrowing model.

title: Worldcoin (WLD) Price Prediction: Can WLD Turn Its $0.40 Liquidity Pool Into a 3,500% Recovery?
summary: Worldcoin (WLD) has returned to a price zone that has attracted attention after a prolonged decline from its 2024 peak.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: WLD

Worldcoin (WLD) has returned to a price zone that has attracted attention after a prolonged decline from its 2024 peak.

Trading around $0.44 in late September, Worldcoin price remains far below its all-time high, while recent price action has shown signs of short-term recovery.

A recent analysis by @0xVertix described the area around $0.40 as a long-term “liquidity pool” following WLD’s roughly 96% decline from its March 2024 peak near $11.82. The analysis suggested that a recovery toward previous highs could represent gains of more than 3,500%, although such a move would require a substantial change in market conditions and demand.

WLD Price Holds Above $0.40 After Sharp Decline

Worldcoin reached an all-time high of about $11.82 in March 2024 before entering a prolonged downtrend. By March 2026, the token had fallen to a new record low near $0.24, according to market data reported at the time.

WLD has fallen about 96% from its March 2024 ATH near $12 to around $0.40, with the prolonged consolidation zone drawing attention amid potential long-term recovery scenarios. Source: @0xVertix via X

Recent data shows that WLD has recovered from that low but remains well below its historical peak. CoinGecko’s historical data shows WLD closing at $0.4579 on September 21, before falling to $0.4065 on September 23. It then recovered toward $0.44 on September 24.

The latest market structure therefore places the $0.40 area between a recent trading range and the token’s longer-term lows. For the bullish thesis outlined by market commentators to develop further, Worldcoin would need to establish sustained demand rather than simply register short-lived rebounds.

The 3,500% figure also requires context. A move from approximately $0.44 to the former $11.82 peak would represent a gain of roughly 2,586%, while a 3,500% increase from $0.40 would place the token near $14.40. Therefore, the percentage cited in the social media analysis represents a broader recovery scenario rather than a straightforward return to the previous all-time high.

Worldcoin OTC Sale Keeps Supply in Focus

Supply dynamics remain an important part of the Worldcoin price outlook. In March 2026, World Assets, a subsidiary of the World Foundation, disclosed $65 million in over-the-counter Worldcoin sales involving four counterparties. The tokens were sold at an average price of approximately $0.27, representing about 239 million WLD.

WLD is consolidating near $0.41 in a triangle pattern, while rising OBV and OI point to potential bullish momentum despite persistent supply pressure. Source: @LeMacroCap via X

The transaction occurred when WLD was trading close to its record low. According to @LeMacroCap, concerns surrounding the OTC sale need to be considered alongside subsequent price action, as WLD later advanced from around $0.27 to a local high near $0.70.

The OTC transaction does not eliminate the broader supply question. However, World continues to release WLD through predetermined schedules. In April 2026, the World Foundation said 4.9 billion token, or 49% of the 10 billion initial supply, had been unlocked, with about 3.3 billion in circulation.

World also announced that the aggregate daily unlock rate would fall by 43% on July 24, 2026, from approximately 5.1 million WLD to about 2.9 million WLD. The reduction applied to both community and team/investor allocations.

This distinction is important when assessing Worldcoin’s long-term supply pressure. The project’s whitepaper states that the initial supply cap is 10 billion WLD and that community tokens are released according to schedules influenced by network growth.

WLD Technical Structure Shows Mixed Signals

Technical analysis presents a more nuanced picture than the long-term recovery thesis alone. A Binance perpetual chart referenced by @LeMacroCap showed WLD consolidating around $0.41 in a triangle formation. Rising On-Balance Volume and Open Interest were highlighted as signs of increasing market participation.

WLD has initial support at $0.3450, with stronger support at $0.3154, while its approach toward the 100-period moving average could support further upside. Source: TradingView

Another TradingView analysis identified a bearish channel on the one-hour chart. It placed initial support near $0.3450 and a stronger support area around $0.3154, where Worldcoin had previously rebounded several times.

The analysis also pointed to the 100-period moving average as a nearby technical reference. A move above the channel’s resistance could alter the short-term structure, while failure to hold the lower support areas would weaken the recovery setup.

The broader technical readings are similarly mixed. Recent indicator data showed WLD trading above several short- and medium-term moving averages, with the 5-, 10-, 20-, 50-, 100-, and 200-period averages generally producing buy readings. However, technical signals vary across timeframes, with the one-month reading remaining more cautious.

WLD Price Prediction: Key Levels to Watch

At around $0.44, WLD is trading close to a cluster of short-term pivot levels. Classic pivot calculations place the central pivot near $0.438, followed by resistance around $0.441, $0.442, and $0.445. Support levels are concentrated around $0.436, $0.434, and $0.432.

Worldcoin (WLD) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

This makes the $0.441-$0.445 area an important near-term test. A sustained move above that zone could place attention on higher resistance levels, while repeated rejection could keep Worldcoin within its recent range.

On the downside, $0.40 remains a psychologically important reference after recent trading activity around that level. Below it, the technical analysis identifies $0.3450 and $0.3154 as more established support zones.

The difference between these levels and the former all-time high illustrates the scale of the recovery required for the 3,500% scenario. A return to the $11.82 peak would already require WLD to appreciate several thousand percent from current levels, while reaching approximately $14.40 would be necessary for a 3,500% gain from $0.40.

Can WLD Recover Toward Its Previous High?

The $0.40 area can be described as a long-term consolidation zone based on the chart structure, but whether it becomes a durable accumulation area cannot be established from price action alone.

WLD’s fundamentals will remain closely tied to adoption of the World network, token distribution, circulating supply, and market demand. The project’s tokenomics also mean that supply will continue entering circulation under predetermined schedules. World says its unlock system extends across 15 years, with the final scheduled tranche occurring well after launch.

Recent price data provides evidence of renewed short-term activity. WLD rose from a September 17 close around $0.384 to approximately $0.458 by September 21, before briefly reaching above $0.47 on September 22. It subsequently fell to around $0.406 on September 23 and recovered toward $0.44 on September 24.

That volatility highlights both sides of the current setup. Worldcoin has demonstrated an ability to rebound sharply from depressed levels, but the token has also experienced rapid reversals within the same period.

For the $0.40 liquidity zone to develop into the foundation of a much larger recovery, WLD would need to maintain higher lows, overcome nearby resistance, and sustain demand as circulating supply expands. A move back toward the 2024 peak would also require a substantially different market environment from the one that produced the prolonged decline.

For now, the technical picture suggests the market is attempting to stabilize above the $0.40 level, while the longer-term Worldcoin price prediction depends on whether improving demand can absorb ongoing token releases and sustain the trend.

content:
DeFi Was Never Going to Get Its Clarity from US Congress

2026-09-25T11:25:47.372+02:00

Friday, 25/09/2026 | 09:25 GMT by Mohammad Akhavannik

  • Mohammad Akhavannik, Managing Director of Newton Foundation, highlights Treasury’s role in shaping AML-type screening requirements affecting decentralised finance.
  • New SEC exemptions impose limits on token fundraising and permissioned venues offering tokenized equities.

Last week’s failed CLARITY Act cloture vote will be read as a setback for crypto. That reading misses where decentralized finance (DeFi) compliance was actually heading.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Investors have been watching legislative headlines while the decisions that will govern DeFi access, sanctions screening, and pre-settlement risk checks get written elsewhere.

CLARITY Doesn’t Set the Rules

The industry treated CLARITY as the moment it would finally get regulatory certainty. The bill was never going to deliver that. It covered a lot of ground, including AML program requirements, protections for developers, and jurisdictional lines defining which agencies would regulate different kinds of cryptocurrencies.

The questions that actually determine how much of DeFi stays open to anyone with a wallet, and how much becomes gated by compliance checks, would continue to be kicked down the road. The bill handed those specifics to agency rulemaking, and for AML-type screening, the relevant agency is Treasury.

A failed vote doesn't pause regulation because CLARITY was never delineating the rules. Treating the failure that way just means DeFi keeps waiting to react to rules it could be helping shape.

The SEC Has Already Shown Us What's Coming

Rulemaking didn’t need CLARITY and won’t wait for it or another bill like it. The SEC has already shown how it plans to regulate the industry. Rather than writing one comprehensive framework, the agency has been issuing narrow, conditional rules one at a time, each with tight limits on who qualifies and how long the relief lasts.

In August of this year, the SEC announced Regulation Crypto Assets, proposing new rules for how crypto projects can raise money by selling tokens. title: How Trading Platforms Compete Beyond Technology
summary:
Retail trading platforms increasingly
compete as mass-market digital services. Users expect multi-device access, a
wide range of markets, built-in analytical tools, and an intuitive interface.
These capabilities are necessary, but as they become a standard part of the
offering, technical features al...
content:
Retail trading platforms increasingly compete as mass-market digital services. Users expect multi-device access, a wide range of markets, built-in analytical tools, and an intuitive interface. These capabilities are necessary, but as they become a standard part of the offering, technical features alone are no longer enough to stand out from the competition. A platform's standing is also shaped by app availability, the quality of user communication, audience reach, brand recognition, and its ability to adapt to the conditions of a given market.

These shifts show up in regulatory research as well. In its 2025 review of trading apps, the UK's Financial Conduct Authority reported that a growing share of retail customers now use desktop and mobile apps to access financial products. According to the 2024 Financial Lives survey, 3% of UK adults used trading apps, and nearly half of those users were between 18 and 34. The regulator also noted an expanding range of products and services available through such apps.

Competing for a mass audience also complicates how companies describe their scale. App downloads, registered accounts, funded accounts, active users, and countries served can all be meaningful, but each one measures something different. Sports partnerships are another marker of public visibility, though they don't prove commercial results. That distinction matters whenever platforms are compared, whether by the companies themselves or by the media.

Technology as the Baseline of the Product

Multi-device access has become a core part of what trading platforms offer. A platform today can combine order placement, market data, notifications, charts, educational materials, and account management in one place. Users expect the same account to work seamlessly across a browser, an installed desktop app, and a mobile device. Multi-channel access is increasingly becoming the expected standard for any major digital service rather than a competitive edge on its own.

IQ Option is an online trading platform that provides access to contracts for difference (CFDs) across several asset classes. The service is available through a web interface, Windows, Mac, Android, and iOS, with the exact product range depending on the user's location. According to the company's current website, the platform launched in 2013. Public market pages on the site group products into categories including stocks, currency pairs, cryptocurrencies, ETFs, commodities, and indices. The analytics section offers historical quotes, economic calendars, and instrument specifications. The specific products and features available to a given user can depend on both their location and the interface they use.

Mobile distribution gives platforms access to a far larger potential audience, but it also changes how that reach gets measured. As of September 2026, IQ Option's Google Play page showed more than 100 million downloads.

Broader access doesn't make every product suitable for every user. The FCA found that some apps placed lower-risk investment products right alongside more complex ones. The regulator expects firms to define their target audience and assess whether customers understand the risks involved. Making access easier expands the potential audience, but it doesn't erase the differences between products or the obligations that come with them.

User Communication as Part of the Product

For a digital trading platform, the relationship with users doesn't end once the app is installed. Support, educational content, notifications, communities, and promotions all become additional touchpoints with the audience. Much of this communication now happens directly inside the product, so the availability of help and educational content becomes part of the overall user experience rather than just external marketing.

IQ Option's Google Play listing advertises round-the-clock support via messages, chat, and free phone calls, along with educational content in the form of video tutorials, emails, and blog articles in multiple languages. That kind of channel mix is no longer unusual for a major digital service — it reflects the expected standard of service and helps build user trust in the platform.

Promotions create another channel for engagement, but they need to be described precisely. IQ Option's official promotions page listed terms in 2026 for a PlayStation 5 Pro giveaway, a series of regional tournaments, and weekly rewards. One giveaway entry was awarded for every deposit of $10 or more made with a promo code. Campaigns like these show how a platform stays in touch with its audience through events and rewards.

Marketing Beyond the Financial Industry

As trading platforms have widened their audience, sports sponsorship has taken on a prominent role in the industry's marketing. According to SportQuake, online trading brands spent $183 million on sports sponsorship in the 2024/25 season — three times what they spent in 2019. The study covered 66 brands and 122 deals, with football and Formula 1 among the most visible categories.

IQ Option has taken a similar approach in motorsport and tennis. DailySportsCar reported on a partnership with Aston Martin Racing in 2016, and GPToday covered its sponsorship of Red Bull Racing in 2018. FinanceFeeds later reported on a collaboration with the Davis Cup in 2022, and Finance Magnates reported that in 2025 IQ Option became an official partner of United Autosports.

These deals confirm brand visibility across different markets and time periods. They show that trading platforms are increasingly tapping the same international marketing channels used by other mass-audience companies in tech and finance.

Adapting to Local Markets

A platform's international presence doesn't mean every customer gets the same product. Local rules, product-specific restrictions, and distribution arrangements can all affect what's on offer and which company is actually providing the service. The FCA found that companies operating trading apps use a range of different business models, and it stressed the need to tell customers when they're contracting with a foreign company or when that affects the protections available to them.

In 2023, FinanceFeeds reported that IQ Option served millions of users in more than 200 countries. That kind of geographic reach doesn't mean users in every market get an identical service. Depending on the country, the range of products and features, the deposit and withdrawal methods and providers involved, the marketing formats, the languages, and the support channels can all differ. In other words, the same platform gets localized based on local rules, distribution arrangements, and audience expectations.

What Shapes a Platform's Competitiveness

These examples show that multi-device access, analytical tools, and a broad product range have become baseline elements of any digital service. They shape the quality of the user experience, but on their own they don't describe a platform's position in the market. When comparable features are available across the industry, competition moves beyond technology.

In that environment, what matters is distribution, user communication, visibility beyond the financial industry, and how well the offering adapts to local rules and audience expectations. Downloads, registrations, active accounts, geographic reach, support channels, promotions, and sponsorship deals each reveal a different facet of that competition — and none of them should be mistaken for the others.

title: Raiffeisen’s 18M-Customer Crypto Push Expands Bitpanda Access Across 11 CEE Markets
summary:
Key Takeaways: Raiffeisen Bank International and Bitpanda are developing a digital-asset-services group-wide framework in Central and Eastern Europe (CEE). Bitpanda Enterprise will be responsible for the infrastructure, which may be
The post Raiffeisen’s 18M-Customer Crypto Push Expands Bitpanda Acc...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Raiffeisen Bank International and Bitpanda are developing a digital-asset-services group-wide framework in Central and Eastern Europe (CEE).
  • Bitpanda Enterprise will be responsible for the infrastructure, which may be extended through RBI’s network of over 18 million customers.
  • The rollout will occur market by market, as a crypto-banking model was first implemented by a Raiffeisen bank in Austria in 2024.

Raiffeisen Bank International (RBI) is taking its crypto strategy beyond Austria, partnering with Bitpanda to build a common framework for digital assets across its Central and Eastern European network. The deal puts crypto closer to the banking apps and financial relationships already used by millions of customers.

  • Bitpanda Infrastructure Behind RBI’s Crypto Expansion
  • Austria Pilot Becomes the Expansion Model
    • Rollout Will Depend on Local Crypto Rules

Bitpanda Infrastructure Behind RBI’s Crypto Expansion

In exchange for the partnership, RBI’s network banks get access to Bitpanda Enterprise, the B2B infrastructure arm of the European crypto platform. The framework won’t mandate banks to create their own technology stack for digital assets, but instead to offer a shared infrastructure layer.

Bitpanda Enterprise claims their institutional technology addresses digital-asset investment infrastructure, liquidity, custody, payments, stablecoins and tokenization. The introduction of services will be a decision for individual RBI banks based on the local markets and regulatory needs.

The group serves 18.8 million customers; RBI has subsidiary banks in 11 CEE markets. Some 18 million customers is the potential regional size of the digital-asset framework, the companies say, not the number receiving crypto services right now.

Read More: ECB Launches Pontes to Move €1.6B Tokenized Market Into Central Bank Money

Austria Pilot Becomes the Expansion Model

It followed a 2024 integration that made Raiffeisen Landesbank Niederösterreich-Wien (RLB NÖ-Wien) one of the first traditional EU banks to offer customers access to crypto via an established banking framework via Bitpanda.

The new arrangement changes the scale of that model. RBI and Bitpanda are creating an integration framework instead of one bank which could be followed by the entire banking ecosystem.

RBI CEO Michael Höllerer said the bank is witnessing increasing demand for crypto assets in its markets and is catering it via its collaboration with Bitpanda.

It’s also evidence of a larger B2B trend in crypto: banks can leverage specialised infrastructure providers instead of building out everything themselves. According to Bitpanda’s research, licensing and ease of integration are key factors for financial institutions when selecting crypto partners.

Rollout Will Depend on Local Crypto Rules

The partnership does not imply that the same crypto products will be available in all 11 markets at the same time.

RBI and Bitpanda said they will implement it in a gradual manner that is customized by the jurisdiction. That’s the actual product and services that will be offered, and the fees (prepaid or recurring) that the customer will pay, for each market launch and not for one single offering regionwide.

For Bitpanda, the deal adds another major banking distribution channel in Europe. For RBI, it provides a common technological foundation for expanding digital-asset services while leaving individual markets to determine how those services are introduced.
